mainTopic: The end of רבי יוחנן's list of לאו הניתק לעשה cases, then lashes for forbidden creatures and for טבל missing מעשר עני
overview: The גמרא finishes testing רבי יוחנן's statement that only a few prohibitions with a fix-it מצוה (לאו הניתק לעשה) still get מלקות. It explains that the משכון of a גר is not on his list because the man still owes money. It then struggles with פאה and concludes that רבי יוחנן's two cases are שילוח הקן and פאה. The אונס is not one of them, because a vow made with the public's consent can be undone for a מצוה, as the story of the reinstated teacher shows. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's forbidden foods. It rules on creatures from plowed furrows, and counts the sets of מלקות for a פוטיתא, an ant and a wasp. It also gives cases of 'לא תשקצו' and explains how crushed ants plus one live ant add up. Finally, רב rules that food missing only מעשר עני is still טבל, based on רבי יוסי's גזירה שוה. רב יוסף then begins a מחלוקת of תנאים on this, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The man who kept the convert's collateral owes money, so he is not lashed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question about the משכון of a גר who died: the borrower is still obligated to pay. Only the גר's claim has lapsed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the man is still someone who owes payment. It is only the convert's lien that has lapsed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from just before this point. Why isn't keeping the collateral of a גר who died on רבי יוחנן's list of cases that get מלקות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower is still a person who owes payment. It is only the גר's claim that disappeared, because there is no heir to collect. Since he is in the category of someone who must pay money, he does not get מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is obligated to pay money
A lien or legal claim on property
Lapsed, disappeared
A convert

phrases.english: There, the man is someone who is subject to payment,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case just before this, where the convert who owned the collateral died.

phrases.english: and it is only the convert's lien that has lapsed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משכון of a גר, which came just before this text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: the person is in the category of one who pays money, so he is not lashed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the מצוה of returning the collateral can no longer be done after the גר dies, the borrower should get מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The borrower is still obligated to pay. Only the גר's claim lapsed, so there are no מלקות.

steps.title: Challenge: פאה should also be on the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings פאה as another prohibition with a fix-it מצוה, and it should get מלקות under both opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is פאה! The תורה says, "Do not finish off the corner of your field," and then, "Leave them for the poor and the convert." This case works under both opinions: 'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it' and 'he nullified it or did not nullify it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's list again. פאה looks like a classic לאו הניתק לעשה, so why didn't he include it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a ban (don't harvest the corner) and a fix-it command (leave it for the poor). The גמרא claims the case fits under both views of when such a לאו gets מלקות: when he fails to do the fix-it מצוה, or when he makes it impossible to do. The proof that it can become impossible comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field that must be left for the poor
A prohibition that has a positive מצוה to fix it
The opinion that lashes depend on whether he did or did not do the fix-it מצוה
The opinion that lashes depend on whether he made the fix-it מצוה impossible

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read קיימו ולא קיימו and ביטלו ולא ביטלו as two cases in פאה. They are two opinions about when a לאו הניתק לעשה gets מלקות, and the גמרא says פאה works under both.

phrases.english: But isn't there the case of the corner of the field,
as the Merciful One said: "You shall not finish off the corner, etc."
"For the poor and the convert you shall leave them, etc."
and you find it under 'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it,'
and under 'he nullified it or did not nullify it'!
phrases.notes: These are the two opinions about when a person gets lashes for this kind of prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the משכון case, the גמרא raises a new case that might be missing from רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that only a few לאו הניתק לעשה cases get מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פאה has a ban plus a fix-it מצוה that can be lost, so it should get מלקות under both opinions. It is missing from the list.

steps.title: Proof that the chance to give פאה can be lost
steps.stepSummary: A teaching lists the stages at which פאה can still be given. This shows that after a certain point, the chance is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The מצוה of פאה is to separate it from standing grain. If he didn't, he separates from the sheaves. If he didn't do that, he separates from the grain pile, as long as he has not yet smoothed it. If he has smoothed it, he takes off the tithes and then gives the פאה to the poor person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a teaching. It traces each stage of the harvest at which פאה can still be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage is a backup for the one before: standing grain, then sheaves, then the pile, then after smoothing (with tithes first). The list ends at the grain pile. So once the grain is ground into flour, it seems פאה can no longer be given. That means the מצוה can be made impossible, which supports the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing grain still growing in the field
Sheaves of cut grain
A pile of threshed grain
Smoothed the pile, the step that makes the grain obligated in tithes
Takes off the tithes

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: מִצְוַת פֵּאָה לְהַפְרִישׁ מִן הַקָּמָה.
phrases.english: As we learned: The מצוה of the corner is to separate it from the standing grain.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִפְרִישׁ מִן הַקָּמָה – מַפְרִישׁ מִן הָעוֹמָרִין.
phrases.english: If he did not separate it from the standing grain, he separates it from the sheaves.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִפְרִישׁ מִן הָעוֹמָרִין – מַפְרִישׁ מִן הַכְּרִי,
phrases.english: If he did not separate it from the sheaves, he separates it from the grain pile,
as long as he has not yet smoothed it.
If he smoothed it, he tithes it and gives it to him!
phrases.notes: "Him" is the poor person. Once the pile is smoothed, tithes come first.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִצְוַת פֵּאָה לְהַפְרִישׁ מִן הַקָּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the פאה challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That the מצוה of פאה can become impossible to do
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that lists the stages for giving פאה, which stops at the grain pile

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows רבי ישמעאל: פאה can be given even from dough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן holds like רבי ישמעאל, who says פאה can be separated even from dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי ישמעאל, who said: One separates פאה even from the dough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. He follows an opinion under which the chance to give פאה lasts much longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, even after grinding and kneading, the farmer can still give פאה from the dough. So grinding does not end the מצוה. That is why פאה is not on the list of cases that get מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough
Even

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yishmael, who said:
He separates it even from the dough.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, דְּאָמַר: אַף מַפְרִישׁ מִן הָעִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פאה challenge from steps 2–3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties רבי יוחנן to a תנא whose view removes the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the grain is ground, the מצוה of פאה is lost, so there should be מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי ישמעאל, פאה can still be given from dough, so the מצוה was not lost.

steps.title: Even for רבי ישמעאל, eating the dough ends the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even according to רבי ישמעאל, the chance to give פאה is lost if the farmer eats the dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even according to רבי ישמעאל you can find such a case: where he ate the dough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. Even with רבי ישמעאל's view, there is still a way to lose the מצוה completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being allowed to give פאה from dough only pushes the deadline later. Once the dough is eaten, nothing is left to give, so the מצוה is truly gone. The question of why פאה is missing from רבי יוחנן's list comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, even
Where he ate

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yishmael too, you find it,
phrases.notes: "It" means a case where the farmer makes the מצוה of the corner impossible to do.

phrases.english: where he ate the dough!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל נָמֵי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, דַּאֲכַל עִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי יוחנן follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if פאה can be given from dough, eating the dough destroys the מצוה. So the case still fits a לאו הניתק לעשה that gets מלקות, and it should be on the list.

steps.title: The 'one more' case is פאה, not the אונס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'this and one more' refers to שילוח הקן and פאה. The אונס does not count, because a vow made with the public's consent can be undone for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'this and one more' refers to this case (פאה), but not to the אונס. When do we say that a vow made with the public's consent can never be undone? Only for an optional matter. For a מצוה, it can be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles which two cases רבי יוחנן meant, and explains why the אונס is not one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the אונס loses his chance to remarry forever if he vowed with the public's consent not to take her back. The גמרא says no: that kind of vow can still be undone when a מצוה is at stake. So his fix-it מצוה is never truly lost, and he does not belong on רבי יוחנן's list.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This and one more': רבי יוחנן's phrase for the only two cases of this kind
A man who violated a girl. He must marry her and may never divorce her
A vow made with the public's consent, which normally cannot be undone
Undoing or cancelling a vow
An optional matter, not a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: A vow made עַל דַּעַת רַבִּים cannot be undone for an optional matter, but it can be undone for a מצוה. That is why the אונס can always remarry, and why the 'one more' case is פאה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the אונס is free of his obligation. He is left off the list because his chance to fix things is never lost.

phrases.english: Rather, 'this and one more' —
refers to this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is פאה, the one the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: but a rapist — no.
For where do we say

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּעַת רַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה –
phrases.english: that a vow made with the public's consent cannot be undone?
For an optional matter,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה – יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה.
phrases.english: but for a מצוה matter, it can be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the back-and-forth over which cases רבי יוחנן's 'this and one more' covers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the cases and narrowing the vow rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אונס who vowed with the public's consent might be the 'one more' case, since his chance to remarry seemed lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'one more' case is פאה. The אונס's vow can be undone for a מצוה, so he is excluded.

steps.title: The teacher who was put back in his job
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא made a vow barring a careless teacher from teaching, but רבינא reinstated him because no one else was as precise. This shows that a vow made with the public's consent can be undone for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of a teacher of young children who was careless with the children. רב אחא made a vow removing him, and רבינא put him back, because no one else could be found who was as precise as he was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real story to prove the rule it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching Torah to children is a מצוה. So even though רב אחא's vow was made with the public's consent, רבינא could undo it. This backs up the rule that such a vow can be undone for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of young children
Was careless or negligent
He made a vow against him (to remove him)
He brought him back, reinstated him

phrases.english: Like that case of a certain teacher of young children
who was careless with the children.
רב אחא made a vow removing him,
and רבינא put him back,
because no one was found who was as precise as he was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the rule from step 6 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: A vow made with the public's consent can be undone for a מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אחא and רבינא and the teacher of children.

steps.title: מלקות for eating the fish-like creature from plowed furrows
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה's list of forbidden foods, רב יהודה rules that someone who eats a small fish-like creature found in plowed furrows gets מלקות for eating a creeping thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who eats נבילות, טריפות, שקצים and רמשים gets מלקות. רב יהודה said: someone who eats the small fish-like creature found in the furrows of a plowed field gets מלקות, because of the verse 'a creeping thing that creeps on the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה about forbidden foods, and רב יהודה gives a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This creature looks like a fish, but it does not come from water. It comes from the ground in the furrows, so it counts as a creature that creeps on the land and is forbidden by that verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that died without proper שחיטה
Animals with a fatal injury or defect
Repulsive creatures and creeping things
A small fish-like creature found in plowed furrows
We give him מלקות (lashes)

phrases.english: 'And one who eats נבילות and טריפות,
repulsive creatures and creeping things, etc.'
רב יהודה said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דַּאֲכַל בִּינִיתָא דְּבֵי כְרָבָא –
phrases.english: Someone who eats the fish-like creature from plowed furrows —
we give him מלקות
because of 'a creeping thing that creeps on the land.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of fix-it מצוות and starts a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating the fish-like creature from plowed furrows earns מלקות under the ban on creatures that creep on the land.

steps.title: רב יהודה actually gave מלקות for it
steps.stepSummary: A man ate this creature, and רב יהודה gave him מלקות, carrying out his own ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man ate the fish-like creature from plowed furrows, and רב יהודה gave him lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing that רב יהודה really carried out his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not just a theory. רב יהודה actually punished someone for it, which shows how seriously he held the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He had him whipped, gave him lashes

phrases.english: A certain man ate the fish-like creature from plowed furrows,
and רב יהודה gave him lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב יהודה putting his ruling from step 8 into practice.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that this creature earns מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man רב יהודה punished.

steps.title: Four sets of מלקות for eating a פוטיתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that someone who eats a פוטיתא, a small sea creature, gets four sets of מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: if someone ate a פוטיתא, he gets lashes four times.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another forbidden-food case, where a single act of eating breaks several prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פוטיתא is a creeping creature of the sea. It falls under two prohibitions about water creatures without fins and scales, and two more about creeping things in general. So one act of eating earns four sets of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A small creeping creature found in the sea
Gets four sets of מלקות

steps.whatToRemember: One act of eating can break several prohibitions at once, and each prohibition can bring its own set of מלקות.

phrases.english: אביי said:
If he ate a פוטיתא —
he gets lashes four times.
phrases.notes: Two prohibitions are for sea creatures without fins and scales, and two are for creeping things in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case to the discussion of forbidden creatures from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a פוטיתא earns four sets of מלקות, one for each prohibition it breaks.

steps.title: An ant brings five sets of lashes and a wasp brings six
steps.stepSummary: אביי's list continues: eating an ant brings five sets of מלקות, and eating a wasp brings six.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ant: he is flogged five times, because of the verse about creatures that creep on the ground. A wasp: he is flogged six times, because of the verse about winged creeping creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues אביי's list from the last step. Each creature carries more sets of מלקות than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ant is not a sea creature, so the two water-creature איסורים from the פוטיתא do not apply. It gets the two general creeping-thing איסורים plus three איסורים about creatures that creep on the ground, making five. A wasp is also a winged creeping creature, which adds one more איסור, making six.

keyTerms.meaning: An ant
A wasp
He is flogged (gets מלקות)
Winged creeping creatures, which the תורה forbids eating

phrases.english: An ant – he is flogged five times,
because of "a creeping thing that creeps on the ground."
A wasp – he is flogged six times,
because of "winged creeping creatures."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's list that began with the פוטיתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ant = five sets of מלקות; wasp = six sets of מלקות.

steps.title: Holding back from relieving oneself breaks לא תשקצו
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי rules that someone who delays going to the bathroom breaks the איסור of לא תשקצו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי said: Someone who holds himself back from relieving himself breaks the איסור of "Do not make yourselves disgusting."
steps.whatsHappening: The verse "לא תשקצו" came up in the creeping-creature rules, so רב אחאי applies it to a new case: making your own body disgusting by holding things in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is not only about eating disgusting creatures. רב אחאי reads it more broadly, as a ban on doing disgusting things to yourself.

keyTerms.meaning: "Do not make yourselves disgusting" – a תורה איסור
One who delays or holds back
His body's openings (here: relieving himself)

phrases.english: Rav Aḥai said:
One who holds back his body's openings
phrases.notes: He means someone who delays going to the bathroom when he needs to.

phrases.english: violates "Do not make yourselves disgusting."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחַאי הַמְשַׁהֶה אֶת נְקָבָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the creeping-creature verses to a broader use of לא תשקצו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delaying relieving oneself breaks לא תשקצו.

steps.title: Drinking from a bloodletter's horn breaks לא תשקצו
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי adds another case of לא תשקצו: drinking from a bloodletter's horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: Someone who drinks from a bloodletter's horn breaks the איסור of "Do not make yourselves disgusting."
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another example of a disgusting act that falls under לא תשקצו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood has passed through the bloodletter's horn, so drinking from it is repulsive. This is the same wider reading of the verse that רב אחאי used.

keyTerms.meaning: A horn
A bloodletter

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
One who drinks
from the horn of a bloodletter
violates "Do not make yourselves disgusting."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי הַאי מַאן דְּשָׁתֵי בְּקַרְנָא דְּאוּמָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second example of לא תשקצו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking from a bloodletter's horn breaks לא תשקצו.
steps.whatToRemember: לא תשקצו covers more than eating creeping creatures. It also forbids doing disgusting things to one's own body.

steps.title: Nine crushed ants plus one live ant bring six sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא rules that eating nine crushed ants plus one live ant, which together make a כזית, brings six sets of מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב הונא said: If someone crushed nine ants, added one live ant to make an olive's size, and ate them, he gets six sets of lashes. He gets five for the whole creature, and one for an olive's size of dead carcass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to ants and describes a mixed case: crushed ants together with one whole live ant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole live ant counts as a complete creature (בריה), so it brings the five sets of מלקות from step 11 even though it is tiny. All the ants together reach a כזית of נבילה, which adds one more, for a total of six.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushed
A whole creature, which is forbidden even if smaller than a כזית
An olive's size, the usual minimum amount for punishment
A dead creature that was not slaughtered properly

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Huna said:
If he crushed nine ants
and brought one live one
and completed them to an olive's size –
he is flogged six times:
five – because of a whole creature,
phrases.notes: This is the live ant, which counts as a full creature. These are the five from the ant rule above.

phrases.english: and one – because of an olive's size of a carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא רִיסֵּק תִּשְׁעָה נְמָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ant from step 11 and builds a combined case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine crushed ants plus one live ant that make a כזית = six sets of מלקות (five for בריה, one for כזית נבילה).
steps.confusionAlert: The five sets come from the one whole live ant, not from the crushed ones. The crushed ants only help reach the כזית for the sixth set.

steps.title: Even two crushed ants, or even one, with the live ant
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, says even two crushed ants with the live one bring six sets of מלקות. רב יוסף says even one crushed ant with the live one does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even two crushed ants plus the live one. רב יוסף said: Even one crushed ant plus the live one.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more opinions use far fewer crushed ants than רבא בר רב הונא's nine. This looks like a disagreement, and the next step deals with that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר רב הונא spoke of nine crushed ants, רבי יוחנן of two, and רב יוסף of one. The numbers clash, so the reader expects the גמרא to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Even two and it (two crushed ants plus the live one)

phrases.english: Rava said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even two and it.
phrases.notes: Two crushed ants plus the one live ant are enough.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Even one and it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֲפִילּוּ שְׁנַיִם וְהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers smaller numbers that seem to clash with step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two crushed ants (רבי יוחנן) or one crushed ant (רב יוסף) plus the live one bring six sets of מלקות.

steps.title: No real disagreement: big ants versus small ants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the opinions do not argue. The smaller numbers are about big ants, and nine is about small ants.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree. This one is talking about big ants, and that one is talking about small ants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the apparent clash between the different numbers of ants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the rule needs a כזית. Big ants reach a כזית with only one or two crushed ants, while small ants need nine. So each אמורא described a different size of ant.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
Big ones
Small ones

steps.whatToRemember: The real requirement is a כזית together with one whole creature. The number of crushed ants just depends on how big the ants are.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this one – with big ones,
phrases.notes: This means רבי יוחנן and רב יוסף, who said one or two crushed ants.

phrases.english: and that one – with small ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי הָא בְּרַבְרְבֵי וְהָא בְּזוּטְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the clash between steps 14 and 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (אוקימתא): big ants versus small ants
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אמוראים disagree about how many crushed ants are needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree that a כזית is needed. The number depends on the size of the ants.

steps.title: רב: missing only poor man's tithe still counts as טבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about eating טבל, and רב rules that eating טבל where only מעשר עני was not taken brings מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who ate טבל or מעשר ראשון' and so on. רב said: if someone ate טבל where only מעשר עני is missing, he gets מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line in the משנה about eating טבל. רב adds a new ruling: even food that is missing only מעשר עני counts as טבל, and eating it brings מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we think of טבל as food that has had nothing taken from it. רב says that even if everything else was taken and only מעשר עני is still inside, the food still has the full status of טבל. That is a big claim, so the גמרא will look for its source next.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required gifts (תרומה and מעשרות) have not yet been separated; forbidden to eat
First tithe, given to the לוי
Poor man's tithe, given to the poor in certain years of the שמיטה cycle
He receives מלקות (lashes)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not talking about food that had nothing taken from it. He means food where everything was separated except מעשר עני, and he still calls it טבל.

phrases.english: "One who ate untithed produce and first tithe," etc.
Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל טֶבֶל שֶׁל מַעְשַׂר עָנִי – לוֹקֶה.
phrases.english: If one ate produce that is untithed only with regard to poor man's tithe, he is flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אָכַל טֶבֶל שֶׁל מַעְשַׂר עָנִי – לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ants discussion and returns to a new line of the משנה about טבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce missing only מעשר עני has the status of טבל, and one who eats it receives מלקות.

steps.title: רב follows רבי יוסי in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion רב follows and answers: רבי יוסי, who asks how we know that food missing even only מעשר עני is considered טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It follows this תנא. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said, You might think a person is only liable for טבל that had nothing at all taken from it. But if תרומה גדולה was taken and not מעשר ראשון, or מעשר ראשון but not מעשר שני, or even only מעשר עני is missing, how do we know he is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא agrees with רב, and points to רבי יוסי in a ברייתא. רבי יוסי sets up the question: how do we know that partly-tithed food is still טבל? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי lists cases step by step, each with fewer gifts missing, ending with only מעשר עני missing. The word 'even' shows that מעשר עני is the hardest case to call טבל. This is exactly רב's case, so רב is following רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom? (Which opinion does this follow?)
One might have thought (introduces a wrong assumption)
The main תרומה, the first gift taken from produce and given to a כהן
Second tithe, eaten by the owner in ירושלים
From where do we know? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei says:
One might have thought that he is not liable
except for untithed produce
from which nothing at all was taken;
if teruma gedola was taken from it
but first tithe was not taken from it,
or first tithe was taken but not second tithe,
or even only poor man's tithe is missing, from where do we know he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the תנא whose view supports רב's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא agrees with רב, and how do we know partly-tithed food is טבל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב follows רבי יוסי in a ברייתא, who holds that even food missing only מעשר עני brings liability.

steps.title: The פסוק that makes food missing מעשר עני forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns from a גזירה שוה on the word 'בשעריך' that 'you may not eat in your gates' includes food still holding מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'You may not eat in your gates...' And elsewhere it says: 'and they shall eat in your gates and be satisfied.' Just as there it means מעשר עני, here too it means מעשר עני. And the תורה said: 'You may not.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives his source. He links two פסוקים that both say 'in your gates,' and shows that the איסור applies to food still holding מעשר עני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק ('they shall eat in your gates and be satisfied') is clearly about מעשר עני given to the poor. Since the first פסוק uses the same words, it is also talking about מעשר עני. So the תורה's 'you may not eat' is a לאו about food whose מעשר עני was not taken, which means מלקות, just like רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the source)
In your gates (the shared word that links the two פסוקים)
Just as there, so too here (the form of a גזירה שוה)
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ / the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Food missing only מעשר עני is still טבל, because of the גזירה שוה of 'בשעריך'. That is the source for רב's ruling of מלקות.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"You may not eat within your gates," etc.
And elsewhere it states:
"And they shall eat within your gates and be satisfied,"
just as there it is speaking of poor man's tithe,
so too here it is speaking of poor man's tithe,
phrases.notes: Here it means food that still has its מעשר עני inside, not yet separated.

phrases.english: and the Merciful One said: "You may not."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's question 'מנין' with a source from the פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That eating food still holding מעשר עני violates a לאו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: גזירה שוה between 'בשעריך' in דברים 12:17 and דברים 26:12.

steps.title: רב יוסף: this is a מחלוקת of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the question is a מחלוקת between תנאים, and begins quoting רבי אליעזר about מעשר עני of דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is like a מחלוקת of תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: one does not need to designate by name the מעשר עני of דמאי. And the חכמים say:
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says that רב's ruling is really a topic that תנאים argue about. He starts quoting the מחלוקת, and the words of the חכמים continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that for דמאי there is no need to designate מעשר עני at all. This suggests that missing מעשר עני does not make food טבל, which is against רב and רבי יוסי. The חכמים's opinion, which comes on the next amud, will be the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a dispute between תנאים
To call the name; to designate a portion as a specific gift
Produce bought from someone not trusted about separating tithes

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is like a dispute between tanna'im.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
One does not need to call the name
phrases.notes: He means you don't have to set aside a portion and say 'this is מעשר עני.'

phrases.english: upon poor man's tithe of doubtfully tithed produce,
And the Rabbis say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding a source for רב, רב יוסף shows the issue is debated among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether food missing מעשר עני is טבל depends on a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about מעשר עני of דמאי.
